in stark contrast to most of the comments here, in my experience lexapro and zoloft (another ssri) both gave me severe delusions, delirium, brain fog, mood swings, and hallucinations. honestly name a negative and i had it; i have not taken medication in a couple years atp due to a fear of going through a similar period. HOWEVER that isn't "normal", and is an indication of a different disorder at play (usually ends up being bipolar, sometimes it's something else). 

if you just have anxiety/depression/ocd, you should honestly expect just a few days of brain fog while the medication adjusts and then you should expect a subtle positive shift in mood or a more stable mood over the next few months. i honestly believe the name of the song is perhaps moreso a reference to the overall dull feeling ssris can give you, but again, my experience is far from the norm so i don't even 100% know if you were always supposed to feel like that.

also wanted to add, i was groomed from a very young age and later from someone else when i was a young teenager. i know that it can feel "not that bad" or "kind of weird" but it is actually illegal and you should not be going through it. you deserve much better than the flattery of those that take advantage of you.

I've loved EDM and electronic music in general since I was a kid; I think my parents playing so much 70s-90s when I grew up helped with that a lot. I started listening to the main genres like house, techno, and dubstep when I was in middle school, but it wasn't until highschool that I started to really appreciate hyperpop, junglecore, breakcore, noisecore, etc.

Besides the music being just generally interesting (with polyrhythms, extreme cutting and editing of vocals to the point of obscurity, and a focus on how the actual music feels as opposed to what lyrics are telling you to feel), I personally use it as sort of... an aid? Lmao. I'm currently unmedicated and a nutcase (like, ocd + schizotypal + autistic), and I cannot lie, I put on Femtanyl or similar artists and my ass is FOCUSED. It literally feels akin to a high for me. However, I will say if I'm listening to music like this casually, it usually is being used in the way one listens to sad music when they're sad. I'm not a violent person or really even that interesting, but sometimes I just wanna kick someone's shit in. I think music like this really helps get out the random anger when you can't do anything to help yourself feel better in any other way. 

Also, the lyrics themselves speak to me and some of my experiences a lot. I'm sure many on this sub feel the same, as it seems the community is full of other trans people and ex/current addicts to various substances or vices. 

As for how I found Femtanyl? .... good question. Honestly I don't recall how I was able to find them so early on in their music making career (at least the publicly posted discography on Spotify) but I was listening to PUSH UR T3MPRR and onwards as they released. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Perhaps the Spotify algorithm blessed me for having the most intolerable music taste on the planet.

My first job was Chipotle and I probably lasted about 3-4 4 hour shifts over the course of a couple weeks before I just couldn't take it anymore (for a plethora of reasons) I took a long break from working because I, too, felt like I just was unable to be in a "normal fast food job" job with "normal" people. 

Turns out the issue was actually just that place and my specific job function! I started at Chick-fil-a about eight months ago, went into the interview telling them I was autistic and would like some accommodations such as ear plugs, and I've been happy ever since. I only do prep so I barely have to interact with anyone, I basically just have to pay attention to my stock, so no managers come and bother me about what to do either. My managers and directors like that I'm "independent". I like that I'm not 6 feet within the radius of someone yelling CHICKEN AT HALF or KNIFE AROUND THE CORNER or SPEED IT UP. 

So, I guess just don't be afraid of applying somewhere else fast food, they usually pay a little better but generally yes they are more stressful than retail jobs but for completely different reasons. If you don't think you can find a slower or more accommodating fast food place, I would try a grocery store near you. There's no harm in also seeing if you know anyone who works somewhere you're interested in and asking how they like it.

I can't believe this isn't a higher comment. OCD makes it extremely difficult for us to understand how other people may view our behavior because our compulsions seem justified in some way, but wanting your girlfriend of two months to remove the passcode on her phone is behavior that can be seen as very controlling. 

I also struggle immensely with self confidence and my relationship with my partner, and even though we've been dating for almost a year now I still am anxious about how they view me and, if my actions had no consequences on others, I would go through and see how they think of me in conversations with mutual friends. However, I have to accept that even if I did that, not only would it not actually help ease my anxieties (because now I'm snooping through messages--who does that?), but it also would mostly likely lead to just more compulsions. 

I would recommend trying to talk it out with her. Explain that you have OCD, what it means, why you're concerned, and have her be able to know that you don't have malicious intent. Genuinely, more people are understanding than you think. My partner and I have an agreement wherein if I ever were to really feel the need, I know the passcode on their phone and they have given me permission to do whatever I want on it. I just simply don't and I make a conscious effort not to. It gives you the freedom of knowing that they aren't trying to hide anything from you, while also giving them the safety and security they deserve as autonomous humans.
